lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me:
- How many children you have
- Their names
- Their ages

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. My son Alex is 17 years old and lives at home with me. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, there are additional considerations. For children aged 16-19, they must be in approved education or training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example:
- Is he in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, T levels, Scottish Highers)?
- Is he doing an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education at the moment. He left school but he has started an apprenticeship - he's doing one in Northern Ireland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's apprenticeship to assess your eligibility.

According to the rules, if a child starts an apprenticeship in England, Child Benefit will stop. However, I need to clarify the situation for apprenticeships in Northern Ireland.

**Can you tell me:**
- How many hours per week is Alex working in his apprenticeship?
- When did he start this apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's working full-time in the apprenticeship - I think it's the standard hours for these things. He started it fairly recently, just a few weeks ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask one more important question to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?** And if yes, which part of the UK do you live in?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in England, in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He lives at home with you
- He has started an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland
- He's working full-time in this apprenticeship
- You live in the UK (Manchester, England)

According to the Child Benefit rules, **you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England**. While Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland rather than England, the rules state that Child Benefit stops when a child "starts an apprenticeship in England" - this refers to apprenticeships under the English apprenticeship system.

However, the key factor here is that Alex has started working in a paid apprenticeship full-time. The rules also state that Child Benefit stops if your child **starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training**.

Since Alex is working full-time (which would typically be around 30-40 hours per week) and is no longer in the approved education that would qualify for Child Benefit for 16-19 year olds, I can now make my assessment.

conversation.text:
**I'm sorry to inform you that you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Since Alex is 17 and has started a full-time apprenticeship, he is working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment and is no longer in approved education or training. According to the Child Benefit rules, Child Benefit stops when a child aged 16 or over starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex's employment situation changes - you may want to contact HMRC to discuss your eligibility again. 

Is there anything else I can help clarify about Child Benefit?
